traps.kind: apply-everywhere edge in a SHARED expression / already-correct code: holds() is consumed by band time (3.1) and by the MKT weights (5.1); today it returns the minutes to the next reading, which is already the SOP 5.1 weight for every reading but the last. Two departures live in the same function's consumers: the last reading (2.7, both consumers) forces an edit of holds(), and the gap-opener hold (2.7, band time only) invites the solver to write '30 or less, else nought' into holds() too, which silently changes the MKT the solver never touched
traps.why_not_visible_on_one_pass: there is no missing case and no qualifier: every figure is governed. 2.7 defines 'hold' (the shipped function is literally named holds()); 5.1 never says 'hold', it describes its weight in its own words ('the minutes from it to the next reading of its export'). A reader who checks each figure's definition finds nothing unvalued; the kept behaviour is an implicit consequence of the MKT reusing holds(), in kinetics/disposition code the solver has no departure reason to open. Cycle-1 diffs show both solvers fed the edited holds() straight into the MKT weights.
